precepts.text: Plead my cause, O Lord, with them that strive with me; fight against them that fight against me. Watch and pray for protection and deliverance, and that none of us drift or get isolated.
precepts.point: Take ye heed, watch and pray, for ye know not when the time is. Stay ready.
precepts.why:
Christ said, “Take ye heed, watch and pray: for ye know not when the time is.” You don't know when the time is coming, so you need to stay prepared, stay ready. The prophecy is unfolding before our eyes: the ten horns giving their kingdoms to the beast, NATO sending weapons and troops here and there, and a time coming when those horns will hate the whore.

So what do we pray for? David shows us: “Plead my cause, O Lord, with them that strive with me: fight against them that fight against me.” Watch and pray for protection and deliverance, asking the Lord to fight against them that fight against us.

Watch and pray that none of us drift, get isolated, or get taken by sin and deception. You can pray for that. These Black Christians don't know what to pray for, but the scripture shows you: pray for the Lord to plead our cause against them that strive with us.

precepts.text: "Say unto my soul, I am thy salvation." Let them be confounded and put to shame that seek his soul; let them be as chaff before the wind and let the angel of the Lord chase them. This applies to our enemies to this day: look at the education systems and the conditions of our people; every nation outside the Israelites is trying to hide a net for our soul.
precepts.point: David asks the Lord to make haste to help him and to put to shame those who seek after his soul to destroy it, and those who say "Aha" to mock him for his transgressions.

note.label: Psalm 40: Patient Waiting, Obedience Over Sacrifice, and the Great Congregation

precepts.why:
“Be pleased, O Lord, to deliver me: O Lord, make haste to help me.” Psalm 35 is the same prayer: “Draw out also the spear, and stop the way against them that persecute me: say unto my soul, I am thy salvation. Let them be confounded and put to shame that seek after my soul: let them be turned back and brought to confusion that devise my hurt. Let them be as chaff before the wind: and let the angel of the Lord chase them. Let their way be dark and slippery: and let the angel of the Lord persecute them.”

Every nation outside the Israelites falls in this category, seeking the heart of the Israelites without cause. It applies to our enemies to this day: look at the education systems and the conditions of our people; every nation outside the Israelites is trying to hide a net for our soul. So we say what David said: say unto my soul, I am thy salvation, and let the angel of the Lord chase them as chaff before the wind.

moments.label: Know Your Enemy: God's Foes & Ours

points: These I'm about to read, those are prayers you should read for the destruction of your enemies. That's what we praying for today.

Plead my cause, O Lord, with them that strive with me: fight against them that fight against me. Take hold of shield and buckler, and stand up for mine help. Let them be confounded and put to shame that seek after my soul. Let their way be dark and slippery: and let the angel of the Lord persecute them. Let destruction come upon him at unawares; and let his net that he hath hid catch himself: into that very destruction let him fall. And my soul shall be joyful in the Lord: it shall rejoice in his salvation.

Let not them that are mine enemies wrongfully rejoice over me. Don't let them rejoice over the Israelites. Let them not say in their hearts, Ah, so would we have it: because you know that's what they're celebrating today. Let them be ashamed and brought to confusion together that rejoice at mine hurt: let them be clothed with shame and dishonour that magnify themselves against me. And my tongue shall speak of thy righteousness and of thy praise all the day long.

note.label: Know Your Enemy: God's Foes & Ours

points: This is the prayer that we all have, especially us as Israel. We want the Most High to fight against those who fight against us. That is a righteous prayer that our forefather David had.

note.label: Psalm 35: Plead My Cause, O Lord

points: No matter what we think, Esau is too strong for us right now. He owns a military. Black people do not own a military. You may be able to fight one and win, but we do not own a military. We are behind enemy lines. They took over this country and we still have not taken it back. The Most High is the only one who is going to save us from that one who is stronger than us. That is what David prophesied about the nation of Israel.

note.label: Psalm 35: Plead My Cause, O Lord

points: False witnesses rise up and lay to our charge things we knew not. That happens with us right now. You have our own brothers claiming we are with the Rosicrucians, sold out to the Illuminati, that we wear purple because we had to choose a color. The most racist people in the world are not going to recruit us. We have our own money; we gave out gold coins worth a million dollars at the 2015 or 2016 Passover.

note.label: Psalm 35: Plead My Cause, O Lord

points: They rewarded evil for good, but when they were sick, David's clothing was sackcloth and he humbled his soul with fasting. That is praying for your enemies and for those that despitefully use and persecute you. You do not go railing for railing. You defend yourself, but you do not turn around and do something wicked back to them. When they were down, David felt their pain just as they had felt it. That is how we have to move.

note.label: Psalm 35: Plead My Cause, O Lord

points: David bowed down heavily as one that mourns for his mother, but in his adversity they rejoiced and gathered themselves together against him.

note.label: Psalm 35: Plead My Cause, O Lord

points: Our feast days are full of hypocrites, people who do not have the betterment of their people at heart. They come to the feast days, the new moons, the sabbaths, and sit there wicked, crept in unawares. It always happens. This is what David was talking about when he spoke of hypocritical mockers in feast.

note.label: Psalm 35: Plead My Cause, O Lord

points: David cries out asking how long the Most High will look on, and asks him to rescue his soul from their destructions.

note.label: Psalm 35: Plead My Cause, O Lord

points: He asks that his enemies not wrongfully rejoice over him nor wink with the eye that hate him without a cause.

note.label: Psalm 35: Plead My Cause, O Lord

points: When we fall or do something, they point and mock, "Aha, aha, I have seen it." No matter what happens, you have to keep the commandments of the Most High and keep your faith in him. When everybody is against you, keep your faith. That is the example David set.

note.label: Psalm 35: Plead My Cause, O Lord

points: David asks the Most High not to keep silence, to stir up himself and awake to his judgment, and to judge him according to his righteousness.

note.label: Psalm 35: Plead My Cause, O Lord

points: He prays that his enemies not say in their hearts, "We would have had it," or "We have swallowed him up," but that they be brought to confusion.

note.label: Psalm 35: Plead My Cause, O Lord

points: There are people not in the body who see what we go through and pray the best for us. Brothers from a lot of different backgrounds saw what we went through as a body and said they pray the best for us. That is a righteous thing to have. But the ones who do not, the prayer is to let them be brought to confusion, along with all the stuff they talk all the time.
